seo.meta_title: Steak 48 Dress Code: What to Wear (and Where It Is)
seo.meta_description: Steak 48's dress code bans athletic wear and revealing clothes and discourages printed tees, sweatshirts and hats. Plus every Steak 48 location.

question: What Is the Steak 48 Dress Code?
quick_answer: Steak 48 has a business-casual dress code for dinner. Its Chicago policy bans athletic wear, excessively revealing clothing and exposed undergarments, and asks guests to skip printed T-shirts, sweatshirts, hats and visors. Collared shirts and sport coats are encouraged. Steak 48 has locations in Beverly Hills, Charlotte, Chicago, Del Mar, Houston, Philadelphia and Phoenix, with Dallas on the way. Policies can vary by location and can change, so check your restaurant's page before you go.

body.heading: What the dress code says
body.text: Each Steak 48 location posts its own dress code. The Chicago policy says athletic wear, excessively revealing clothing and exposed undergarments aren't allowed, and that the restaurant prefers guests skip printed T-shirts, sweatshirts, hats and visors. It says it always appreciates collared shirts and sport coats and encourages guests to get dressed up. Steak 48 also says management can change or update the dress code at any time.

body.heading: What to wear
body.text: A safe outfit for men is a collared or button-down shirt with slacks or dark jeans and dress shoes, with a sport coat optional. For women, a dress, a nice blouse with trousers or a skirt, or a dressy jumpsuit all fit. Avoid gym clothes, sweatshirts, ball caps, graphic tees and anything very frayed or revealing.

body.heading: The 2021 controversy
body.text: In May 2021, Steak 48 drew national attention after its Philadelphia location posted a $100-per-person food and beverage minimum, before tax and tip, along with a long, detailed dress code that banned items such as tank tops, excessively frayed clothing and clothing with strong odors. Critics said the policy could be enforced unfairly, and the company said it applies the same business-casual standard at all its fine-dining restaurants. It later apologized and said it would add diversity and inclusion training. The current location pages we checked don't mention a spending minimum, so ask when you book.

body.heading: Steak 48 locations
body.text: Steak 48 was started by brothers Jeffrey and Michael Mastro, of the Mastro's steakhouse family, and is run by their Scottsdale-based company, Prime Steak Concepts. The name nods to Arizona, the 48th state. The first Steak 48 opened in Houston in 2016. Today there are locations in Beverly Hills and Del Mar, California; Charlotte, North Carolina; Chicago; Houston; Philadelphia; and Phoenix. A 14,000-square-foot Dallas restaurant is planned for the Knox-Henderson area at McKinney and Monticello avenues.

body.heading: What to order
body.text: Steak 48 is known for USDA Prime, dry-aged and Wagyu steaks, a raw seafood tower, its Chef's Cut Hanging Bacon, Colossal Shrimp Cocktail, Corn Crème Brûlée and Caviar Cones. Many items are priced at market, and it's a special-occasion bill. The full bar opens at 4 p.m. See our Steak 48 menu for details.

faqs.q: Does Steak 48 have a dress code?
faqs.a: Yes. It's business casual for dinner, with no athletic wear, revealing clothing or exposed undergarments.

faqs.q: Can you wear jeans to Steak 48?
faqs.a: Nice, dark jeans with a collared shirt are generally fine. Avoid frayed or ripped denim.

faqs.q: Can you wear a hat at Steak 48?
faqs.a: Hats and visors are discouraged under the dress code.

faqs.q: Does Steak 48 have a minimum spend?
faqs.a: Some locations posted a $100-per-person minimum in 2021. Current pages don't mention one, so ask when you book.
